why_use_this: Reach for this package when your data has more than 2 dimensions -- an image batch, a 3D grid of samples, a stack of matrices -- and [vani-matrix](https://github.com/enthusiasticgeek/vani-matrix)'s fixed rank-2 `(rows, cols)` shape genuinely can't represent it. A tensor here is just a flat row-major `Vec<f64>` plus an explicit `Vec<i64>` shape, with no hidden metadata and no wrapping struct, deliberately matching vani-matrix's own flat-`Vec`-plus-explicit-dims convention -- a rank-2 tensor's data is byte-for-byte a vani-matrix matrix, so you can pass one straight into the other's functions with zero conversion. If your data is genuinely 2D (or 1D), stay with vani-matrix -- it's the more specialized, more direct tool for that case, and this package's indexing/stride machinery is pure overhead you don't need.

math_notes.tensor_size: \( \text{size} = \prod_{d} \text{shape}[d] \) -- total element count, the product of every axis length.
math_notes.tensor_strides: Row-major ("C order") strides: \( \text{stride}[n-1] = 1 \), and \( \text{stride}[d] = \text{stride}[d+1] \cdot \text{shape}[d+1] \) for \( d = n-2, \ldots, 0 \) -- the last axis varies fastest, matching NumPy's default layout.
math_notes.tensor_flat_index: \( \text{flat} = \sum_{d} \text{idx}[d] \cdot \text{stride}[d] \) -- converts a multi-index \( (i_0, i_1, \ldots, i_{n-1}) \) into the single flat offset into the underlying `Vec<f64>`, given the strides `tensor_strides` computes.
math_notes.tensor_unflatten_index: The inverse of `tensor_flat_index`: given a flat offset and the shape, recovers the multi-index \( (i_0, \ldots, i_{n-1}) \) by successive division/modulo against each axis length, most-significant (slowest-varying) axis first.
math_notes.tensor_sum: \( \sum_i a_i \) over every element, treating the tensor as a flat sequence regardless of its shape.
math_notes.tensor_mean: \( \dfrac{1}{n}\sum_i a_i \) -- `tensor_sum` divided by the element count.
math_notes.tensor_contract_last_first: Tensor contraction of \( A \)'s last axis against \( B \)'s first axis (requiring \( A_{\text{shape}}[\text{last}] = B_{\text{shape}}[0] = K \)): \( C_{\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j}} = \sum_{k=1}^{K} A_{\mathbf{i},k} \, B_{k,\mathbf{j}} \), the N-D generalization of matrix multiplication. Because of this package's row-major layout, \( A \)'s data is already exactly an `(outer_A x K)` matrix and \( B \)'s is already exactly a `(K x inner_B)` matrix, so this function reuses [vani-matrix](https://github.com/enthusiasticgeek/vani-matrix)'s `mat_mul_rect` directly under a shape-computing wrapper rather than reimplementing the sum.
